findings.evidence: `rg -n "hermite_eq_deriv_gaussian|coeff_hermite|T_eval_neg|aeval_neg_hermite"` shows Mathlib uses `Polynomial.hermite_eq_deriv_gaussian`, `Polynomial.coeff_hermite_*`, and `Polynomial.Chebyshev.T_eval_neg`, while this PR adds `theorem aeval_neg_hermite ... : aeval (-x) (hermite n) = ...`; the naming guide says theorem names describe the conclusion using adjacent-declaration consistency.
findings.fix: Rename it to a family-first name such as `hermite_aeval_neg` and update the use in `hermiteFunction_neg`.
findings.issue: `aeval_neg_hermite` puts the evaluator before the special polynomial family, unlike the adjacent public Hermite API and Mathlib's analogous Chebyshev parity names.

summary: One public theorem name does not follow the adjacent Mathlib Hermite/Chebyshev naming pattern for special-polynomial evaluation lemmas.
